extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, representatives, and KIPO examiners (Republic of Korea)
extracted.subtask_short: korean patent expedited examination and overseas filing
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules under the Korean Patent Act (and Enforcement Decrees) on (1) prohibition/permission for filing patent applications overseas for national-defense-related inventions and (2) eligibility, request, and documentary requirements for expedited examination (including prior-art search and comparative explanation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications banned from filing overseas
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Article 41 of the Patent Act, inventions crucial for national defense can be banned from filing overseas and may only be filed abroad with government permission; filing abroad without permission is deemed abandonment of the right to obtain a patent and may require compensation for losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications classified by a KIPO examiner as confidential or indicated by the applicant as national defense-related, or those deemed necessary to be kept confidential after consultation with the Defense Acquisition Program Administration, are subject to the ban.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to file a banned application overseas (general process)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention banned from filing overseas may exceptionally be filed abroad when the Korean government grants permission; for the US there is an agreement limiting permitted filings to the Republic of Korea and the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain permission to file in the United States an applicant must submit a written request (Annexed Form No.21) under the Enforcement Rules; KIPO consults with the Defense Acquisition Program Administration and may issue written permission with specific conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions imposed when permission to file in the United States is granted
rubrics_metrics.description: Where permission to file in the US is granted, (1) the specification must be clear and specific to allow examination by US authorities, and (2) the right to claim damages caused by confidentiality of the invention in the US must be waived (except damages from unauthorized US use/disclosure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant who files in the US after permission must attach two copies of application documents, a copy of the Korean permission, personal information and security-cleared representative documentation to the Commissioner of the Defense Acquisition Program Administration, and designate a US security-cleared representative to handle patent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling US-filed national defense-related applications in Korea
rubrics_metrics.description: A US application kept confidential as national-defense-related may be filed in the Republic of Korea by submitting specified copies and documents and a copy of the US permission; KIPO will keep the application confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit two copies of the application, three copies of specification/abstract/drawings (one specification copy may omit the invention description), a copy of US-issued permission for filing in Korea, and relevant security-related documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory grounds for expedited examination (Article 61)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may instruct an examiner to prioritize examination if (1) a person other than the applicant is commercially/industrially practicing the claimed invention after its laying-open, or (2) it is deemed necessary to urgently process an application specified by Presidential Decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the high-level authorization enabling expedited examination; further detail and eligible categories are provided in the Enforcement Decree (Article 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: defense industry applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application directed to the art of the defense industry is eligible for expedited examination under Article 9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among the list of application types the Commissioner may designate for priority handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: green technology
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application directly related to green technology (technologies that minimize greenhouse gases/pollutants, improve energy/resource efficiency, clean energy, recycling, eco-friendliness and related convergence tech) is eligible for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Green technology was added to support Low-Carbon, Green Growth policies; where special institution search results are provided, such applications may be eligible for super-expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: export promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications directly related to export promotion are eligible for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to promote industrial/trade objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: official duties of State or local governments (and national/public schools tech transfer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications relating to official duties of the State or local governments (including patents concerning duties of national and public schools filed by their technology transfer/commercialization offices) are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since July 1, 2005, applications filed by technology transfer offices within national/public schools are treated as government-duty-related for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: applications filed by venture businesses and technology-innovative SMEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed by enterprises confirmed as venture businesses or selected as technology-innovative small and medium enterprises are eligible for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific statutory references: Article 25 (venture), Article 15 (technology-innovative SME). Eligibility can depend on confirmation of status between request and determination times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: companies exemplary in employee invention compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed by enterprises selected as exemplary companies regarding employee invention compensation systems (under Invention Promotion Act Article 11-2) are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added to encourage appropriate employee invention compensation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: results of State projects or quality certification
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application relating to results of State projects supporting new technology development or to quality certification is eligible for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers government-funded R&D outcomes and certification-related inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: application serving as basis of priority claim under treaties
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application which serves as the basis of a priority claim under treaties is eligible if a foreign application claiming priority to it is pending before a foreign patent office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to cases where a foreign patent application claiming priority is pending abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: invention being practiced or prepared to be practiced by the applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application whose invention is being practiced or is being prepared to be practiced by the patent applicant is eligible for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant, a licensee, or authorized practitioner is practicing or preparing to practice the invention (within the Republic of Korea for foreign applicants), the application may be accepted for expedited processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: electronic transaction related applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application directly related to electronic transaction is eligible for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers inventions pertaining to electronic commerce/transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: bilateral/foreign-office agreement for expedited examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application for which the Commissioner of KIPO has agreed with the commissioner of a foreign patent office to expedite examination is eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports cooperative acceleration between offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: authorized prior art search institute result
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application for which a requester requested an authorized prior art search institute (designated under Article 58(1)) to conduct a prior-art search and to notify KIPO of results is eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such prior-art search results can be used to justify necessity of urgent processing; the authorized institute's notification is one basis for acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible category: applicants over 65 or with serious health conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application filed by a person over 65 years of age or by a person not expected to be able to perform patent-related proceedings up to decision due to serious health conditions may be eligible for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies unless they can obtain expedited examination by other means; protects vulnerable applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request expedited examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone, including the applicant, may request expedited examination. However, only central or local governments (including technology transfer offices of national/public schools) may request expedited examination for government-duty-related patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal representatives act for minors/incompetents; unincorporated associations may request under their representatives. Foreign-filed applications can be requested for expedited examination and judged by same criteria as Korean-filed ones (but practicing by a foreigner means practicing within Korea).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications eligible by filing date and utility model rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications and applications for utility model registration filed after October 1, 2006 are eligible for expedited examination; utility model applications filed before that date are not, except converted (dual) applications where a patent is filed based on pre-2006 utility model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requester must have already filed a request for substantive examination; expedited examination applies only where exam request has been or is filed before or at the time of requesting expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference time for determining eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility is determined based on status either at the time of the request for expedited examination or at the time when eligibility is determined; certain qualifications (e.g., venture company status) may be confirmed between request and determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: an applicant becoming a venture company between request and determination can render the application eligible; similarly, change in third-party practicing status may affect eligibility (if third-party stopped practicing by determination time, eligibility may still be recognized if practiced at request time and vice versa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims requirement for eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention that makes the application eligible for expedited examination must be recited in the claims. If the invention is described only in the specification and not claimed, the application is not recognized as eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is assessed based on the claims as amended before the time of determining eligibility. If at least one claim is recognized as eligible, the entire application may be accepted for expedited examination. If eligibility-creating claims are cancelled before determination, the request will not be recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laying-open/publication requirement for third-party practicing basis
rubrics_metrics.description: For the ground that a third party is practicing the claimed invention (Article 61(1)), the application must have been laid open; except for this ground, publication is not required to seek expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request based on third-party practice is filed before laying-open and laying-open is imminent, determination of eligibility may be deferred (not dismissed); once laid open, examiner proceeds with expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of urgent processing: when required and assessment factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications listed under Article 9 are in principle deemed necessary for urgent processing; for other statutory sources (special acts), necessity must be shown. Determination considers (1) relevance to national policies, (2) protection of applicant’s interest, and (3) whether urgent processing is likely to ensure grant of the patent (patentability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For factor (3) the requester can submit prior-art search results and an explanation of patentability comparing the claimed invention to prior art; those materials help the examiner decide urgency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using prior-art search results to establish urgency
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester may submit prior-art search results and a comparative explanation showing why urgent processing is necessary (e.g., demonstrating patentability compared to closest prior art); where an agreement with a foreign office or an authorized institute search exists, the requester may omit duplicate explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When prior-art searches are submitted, the examiner can utilize them for substantive examination and may recognize the application as requiring urgent processing without additional explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents and format for self-search results and contrastive explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: The written explanation must describe the search process and provide a contrastive explanation between the claimed invention and the closest prior-art documents; in principle disclose more than four closest prior-arts, but fewer may be acceptable in new technical fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrastive explanation should sequentially describe similarities, differences, and analysis between each claim (all independent claims require contrastive explanation; dependent claims may be omitted). If an independent claim lacks its own contrastive explanation but is substantially analyzable from another independent claim’s explanation, it may be deemed appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution of search results from local IP centers or additional searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Search results produced with support of local IP centers or additional relevant search results may be submitted instead of the self-search process and results, but a contrastive explanation must still be provided in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such substitutions are acceptable where they sufficiently explain the search and comparison to the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling deficient or missing self-search results/contrastive explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: If self-search results and contrastive explanation are not submitted or are inappropriately disclosed, the examiner will order supplementation; failure to comply or continued inadequacy may result in rejection of the request for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inappropriate disclosure means missing mandatory contents (e.g., search processes, more than four results, independent claims, or contrastive explanations). However, an examiner's later identification of prior art that defeats novelty/inventive step does not by itself prove the self-search was inappropriate. Sufficiency is judged on whether the examiner can easily comprehend the results/explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference on processing time when certain documents impede notification
rubrics_metrics.description: When documents are received that the examiner cannot respond to (e.g., report of change of applicant/representative, resignation of representative), processing time is calculated excluding the period from receipt to the acceptance of those documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if expedited decision made Feb 1, report change submitted Mar 20, and application accepted after amendment Apr 20, the processing time excludes the interval between receipt and acceptance of the report.
